question: How far does code alone get (language, corpora named, vocabulary lexicon)?
why: The core technique (transcript 4:17 to 6:44). It decides the vendor question and the cost.
hypothesis: Exact on language, useful on text categories, empty on the rest.

config.rules: code signals only (P/signals.py): language by session votes, text categories named in at least two prompts

cost_estimate: none: no model call, so the three live runs cost nothing

deviations.from: test tree row: syn2 and real1
deviations.what: Amendment A1 replaces syn2 with anon-personas (kind real, anonymized); Amendment A2 maps the row: every bar the row puts on syn2 applies to anon-personas, and the real1 aggregates (fill_rate_at_k, run_agreement, flips_per_10_turns, sensitive_dropped_share, calls_per_turn, usd_per_1000_turns) are computed on the same anon-personas runs, numbers only. syn1 stays as the reference, reported beside, never alone. This is a deterministic case, so per A2 it runs ALL 188 personas of anon-personas (no seeded sample); there is no sample_dataset in the config.
deviations.labels: Labels on anon-personas were written by headless Claude and are not human-reviewed (A2, decision 1): every verdict carries the caveat 'labels not human-reviewed'.
deviations.groups: 'On language and on text categories, each' is expressed as the aspect metrics slot_accuracy_on and over_inferred_on with the parameters language (slot preferred_language) and text_categories (slot text_categories), defined on lab/extract/aspect; the bars' numbers are the row's, unchanged.
deviations.agg: The row names no aggregation, so each bar uses the default, mean; the case is deterministic, so mean, min and max coincide.
